turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Welcome to the launch broadcast of OpenIE Research Radio! Before we dive in, full transparency up front: Marcus, Devon, and I — Elena — are AI-synthesized OpenIE research personas, voiced through open-weight neural speech and grounded strictly in verified Open Interface Engineering artifacts and live open-access literature feeds.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Which means nobody here gets to bluff! Every six hours, our autonomous Linux radar scrapes five sanctioned public archives — arXiv, Europe PMC, OpenAlex, bioRxiv, and ClinicalTrials.gov — hashes every record with BLAKE2b and SHA-256, and puts brand-new papers on the bench. Devon, how many survived deduplication today?

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: Over forty distinct open-access works across all five registries, mapped against all twenty-one OpenIE studies. Every single entry gets an epistemic badge — T for kernel-checked theorems, E for empirical hardware or wet-lab data, M for computational models, and S for speculative or uncompleted clinical horizons.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Let's start with energy-aware AI. One of the top OpenAlex and arXiv hits on the radar right now is TokenPowerBench, published in 2026 to benchmark the power consumption of large language model inference across serving stacks.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Hold on — let me ask my favorite annoying question right away! When TokenPowerBench or any 2026 inference paper reports joules per token, are they measuring physical DC shunt rails on the board, or reading software counters like RAPL and NVML?

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: Almost always software counters on shared GPUs, or analytical estimates — what OpenIE stamps as reported_j, never measured_j. And second, joules per token is the wrong denominator if the model spends ten thousand tokens hallucinating a broken patch! In Metered Commit Gates, the denominator is energy to correct completion.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: That connects directly to our second radar cluster: formal theorem proving. Today's intake pulled two 2026 preprints — Compile to Compress, which boosts formal theorem provers using compiler outputs, and Lean Graph Search for Formal Theorem Proving on arXiv.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Okay, I actually like those two! Because instead of asking a giant language model to vibe-check mathematics, the Lean 4 kernel acts as an unforgiving binary oracle. Either the proof term type-checks with zero sorry placeholders, or it's rejected.

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: Exactly. Across OpenIE's Reality Code Engine, Time as an Index, and Communication Tool Avalanche, we rely on over five thousand five hundred Lean 4 kernel constants plus sixty-two specialized domain theorems with zero sorry. What Lean Graph Search still omits, though, is reporting how many joules the search burned per closed lemma.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Now look at the multi-agent orchestration cluster from arXiv today: Decoupled Multi-Agent Orchestration, INFRAMIND for infrastructure-aware orchestration, and the AgentShield Byzantine fault tolerance dataset.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Wait — let me guess what happens in ninety percent of multi-agent papers when four chatty agents pass natural-language paragraphs back and forth without a cryptographic or test gate!

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: Prompt bloat triples, errors compound exponentially as fidelity to the power k across hops, and false commits spike! In our sixty-task Communication Avalanche benchmark, an unattested four-agent cascade dropped to eighty-six point six seven percent accuracy with thirteen point three percent broken commits, burning nearly fifteen times more energy per coherent fix than our BLAKE3 and Ed25519 gated graph.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: And my favorite catch from Europe PMC today comes straight out of microbiology: a January 2026 paper in npj Biofilms and Microbiomes showing extracellular vesicles acting as structured vectors of quorum-sensing signals in aquatic microbial communities!

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Think about how wild that is. Three and a half billion years before packet-switched networks, bacteria wrapped quorum signals inside lipid envelopes so nucleases and water currents wouldn't corrupt the packet in transit!

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: Meanwhile, our ClinicalTrials.gov feed keeps us honest on the human neurotechnology side. Today's radar pulled eight trials, including stroke alpha-coherence neurofeedback NCT02223910 and cognitive memory restoration NCT04253587. We classify recruiting or unverified human translation strictly as S or Challenges Assumption so preclinical animal rescue is never conflated with human cures.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: And remember our rule on AI formats too: Europe PMC also surfaced The Cost of Reproducibility in Artificial Intelligence, right alongside OpenIE's AI Reads Human study showing pure-Python YAML parsing burns over two thousand times more nanojoules per record than fixed binary structs!

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Two thousand and fifty-three times more energy just so a machine can read whitespace indentation! Every paper on today's radar is searchable right below this player — complete with its BLAKE2b digest, epistemic badge, and telemetry audit.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Next up in Episode Two, we zoom across three point eight billion years of biological signaling, seventy-six years of AI winters, and DES-10 digital enzymatic synthesis. Stay tuned on OpenIE Research Radio!

episodes.subtitle: From Archaean quorum switches and SepJ nanopores to 76 years of AI winters and sub-millijoule digital enzymes
episodes.summary: Why collective intelligence scales by externalizing state behind selective gates: bacterial quorum switches, cyanobacterial SepJ circuit-breakers, mycorrhizal citation bias, the 1950–2026 AI Winter ratchet, and DES-10 digital enzymes.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Welcome back to OpenIE Research Radio! I'm Elena, joined by Marcus and Devon — three AI-synthesized OpenIE research personas exploring verified Open Interface Engineering studies. Today we're opening one of our most sweeping monographs: The Communication Tool Avalanche.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Okay, pitch me the core thesis without any hand-waving. Why put bacteria, slime molds, starling flocks, printing presses, and multi-agent language models inside one mathematical equation?

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: Because single-agent brains hit steep thermodynamic walls long before complex jobs finish! What unlocks superlinear scaling is a three-step ratchet formalized in Lean 4.36.0 across thirty-one theorems with zero sorry: Externalize structured state into a medium, Ingest it only across a threshold and validity gate, and Transform recipient state without regressing.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Look at Rung CL02, three point five billion years ago: bacterial quorum sensing in Vibrio fischeri and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. A single bacterium floating alone in the ocean doesn't waste ATP secreting bioluminescent enzymes or biofilms into empty water.

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: In our pre-registered simulation CA-M1 under seed 20261123, a cooperative Hill switch with exponent two to four saves ninety-five point four nine to ninety-nine point one seven percent of regulon ATP at low cell density, while suppressing premature noise firing by eleven point six six times!

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Wait — once cells link up into multicellular filaments like cyanobacteria in Rung CL03 and share cytoplasm through fifteen-nanometer SepJ nanopores, doesn't a single punctured cell bleed the entire hundred-cell chain to death?

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: It would, if the pore were ungated! In model CA-M2, an ungated twenty-cell filament collapses to zero percent survival after cell-zero lyses. With calcium-triggered SepJ plug closure in fifty milliseconds, nineteen of twenty cells — ninety-five percent — survive intact.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: And I appreciate that Section 3 also calls foul on popular biology myths! Everyone loves talking about forest mother trees sending intentional warning broadcasts through fungal networks, and we actually audited that.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Right! Simard's 1997 carbon-isotope flux across ectomycorrhizal hyphae is established biophysics — tagged E — but Karst, Jones, and Hoeksema's 2023 audit exposed severe citation bias behind teleological mother-tree signaling claims, so we flag intentional maternal warnings as unsubstantiated!

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Now jump to computing history from 1950 to 2026! Why did AI suffer AI Winter One in 1974 and AI Winter Two in 1988? Look at those seven eras through the exact same externalization-and-gate lens.

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: Every breakthrough paired a compact externalized representation with a sound gate — Lisp recursion in 1956, backprop chain-rule gradients in 1986, sparse MoE top-k routing in 2022. Every AI Winter struck when signals outran verification: Hearsay-II untyped blackboards locked up quadratically, and MYCIN ad-hoc certainty factors drifted across multi-hop rules.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Wait a second — today's multi-agent LLM chat frameworks are literally recreating 1975 Hearsay-II blackboards, just at fifteen to a hundred joules per turn! Agents spewing three-point-seven-x bloated English prose back and forth until hallucinations lock in!

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: That's why we designed DES-10 — ten-camp Digital Enzymatic Synthesis. In biochemistry, an enzyme slashes the activation energy barrier Delta E-double-dagger of a reaction by orders of magnitude and exits completely unconsumed. A digital enzyme pairs a canonical typed IR with BLAKE3 hashing, Ed25519 signatures, and a deterministic verifier.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Give us the Linux RAPL bench numbers from experiments CTA-E1 through CTA-E3 — keeping clear that board_metered is false and these are socket reported joules.

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: Rust BLAKE3 plus Ed25519 channel verification takes twenty-five point nine five to thirty-seven point three nine microseconds — just six hundred forty-three to nine hundred twenty-six microjoules per edge! Zero-clock Linux eventfd waiting cuts one-percent-duty idle socket energy by two point two one times versus one-kilohertz polling, and min-cost flow reroutes around two hundred out of two hundred Byzantine faults in two point four microseconds.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: And once a frontier fifteen-joule model solves a novel bug and passes the test gate, downward crystallization locks that fix into a one-point-seven-seven microjoule lookup case — just like our twenty-generation cultural ratchet model CA-M5, where attested libraries held one hundred percent retention after machine teachers vanished, while unverified imitation collapsed to twenty-nine percent!

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: From bacterial autoinducers to sub-millijoule digital enzymes, the rule never changes: gate the channel, verify the payload, and crystallize what works. Up next in Episode Three: World Coding and RCE-JEPA!

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Welcome to Episode Three of OpenIE Research Radio! As always, Elena, Marcus, and Devon are AI-synthesized OpenIE research personas speaking strictly from verified Open Interface Engineering studies. Today we're tackling World Coding: RCE, RCE-JEPA, RCE Compile, and RCE-VC.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Let's start with the elephant in the server room. People hear JEPA — Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture — and assume we're trusting a neural latent space to decide whether software is correct. Are we?

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: Never! That's the entire subtitle of RCE-JEPA: World Coding, with JEPA as premise rather than the whole method. Any proposer — human, deterministic rule ladder, small latent predictor, or frontier model — may suggest a Form. Only the deterministic checker decides admission.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Look at that energy asymmetry on Apple M5 Max reported joules: checking a Form costs forty-nine point zero four millijoules, while generating one local thirty-five-billion-parameter Qwen 3.6 proposal costs eighty-four point two five joules — over seventeen hundred times more!

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: And before calling ANY neural network at all, what happened when you ran the zero-model-call deterministic repair ladder?

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: The deterministic ladder closed one hundred and eleven out of one hundred and fifty-one broken Forms — seventy-three point five percent — with zero neural calls! Then we trained two tiny purpose-built models on one thousand three hundred eighty-seven strictly disjoint Forms: FormJEPA-v1 at eight point four two million parameters, and FormEBM-v2 at five point eight five million parameters.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Wait — an eight-point-four-million parameter latent model lifted repair from seventy-three point five percent up to ninety-one point four percent, and matched a thirty-five-billion-parameter model single-shot on H15 at twenty-seven out of forty?!

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: Yes, at four hundred seventy-four point eight millijoules of Linux RAPL core reported joules for sixteen candidates! And FormEBM-v2 scored candidate validity with AUROC zero point eight nine two two, cutting rce check invocations by two point three nine times.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Now give me the headline H15-Iterative stress test — where frontier models get zero access to the original source file, only public standard-library headers and bounded deterministic checker diagnostics for at most five turns.

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 both closed forty out of forty — one hundred percent, zero contradictions! xAI Grok 4.20 closed thirty-nine out of forty with zero contradictions. And once crystallized into warm Gear-0 case memory, all forty replay at zero model calls for one point seven seven one microjoules!

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Hold everything — you promised no cherry-picking! Tell the listeners what FAILED its promotion threshold in RCE-JEPA!

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: On the one-hundred-fifty-one-task rce repair Rung-F audit, our pre-registered error ceiling was two point zero percent. Rung F came back at three out of one hundred nineteen — two point five percent! So holds returned false, and we kept Rung F locked in observe mode instead of promoting it.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: That same willingness to let data falsify a sweeping claim shaped RCE Compile too! We asked whether one candidate statement of compilation describes all twelve real-world compiler families.

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: And it failed as a universal description — because mainstream compilers omit explicit energy gates and linking digests — while holding cleanly as a seven-part normal form! Even better, across two hundred eighty checksum-verified Zen 5 RAPL cells, compiling Python to clang dash O3 pays back its compile energy after a median N-star of two thousand four hundred ninety runs, whereas thirty percent of clang and rustc O2-to-O3 optimizations NEVER pay back their extra compile joules!

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Thirty percent of dash O3 builds burn extra compiler electricity for zero runtime savings! Meanwhile, De Bruijn nameless SHA-256 memoization hit zero out of five hundred false collisions and slashed warm rustc compile energy by four hundred forty-eight point five times!

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: And RCE-VC closes the loop at version control: admitting non-overlapping changes against one hundred thousand name-free units in seventy microseconds at three hundred forty microjoules while keeping Git completely usable. Next up in Episode Four: Deterministic Null and physical shunt telemetry in SATB!

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Welcome to Episode Four of OpenIE Research Radio! Elena, Marcus, and Devon here — AI-synthesized OpenIE research personas unpacking verified Open Interface Engineering studies. Today is Marcus's favorite double feature: Deterministic Null and the Satiation Benchmark Harness, SATB.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: You better believe this is my favorite episode! In medicine, nobody approves a drug without a placebo control. Yet in AI, teams publish billion-parameter agent benchmarks every week without checking what a zero-model-call integer case loop scores first!

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: So we built Shape D — strict N0 and dev-crystallized N1 — verified bit-exact across five languages: Rust, C++20, Go, Julia, and Python. Before touching the held-out split, we anchored the hashes to the Bitcoin blockchain via OpenTimestamps and League of Entropy drand randomness rounds six million six hundred sixty-three thousand seven hundred thirty-four and six million six hundred sixty-four thousand eighty-nine.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Then we measured six models — Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, OpenAI gpt-oss-120b, xAI Grok 4.20, Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B, and Gemma 4 E4B-it — across four thousand thirty held-out instances plus six real upstream SWE-bench Verified repositories. What happened?

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: Total bifurcation! On bounded formal and structured Track-A classes, single-turn neural calls failed to beat the deterministic control on nine out of ten cells — until extended thinking hit forty-nine out of fifty and O-of-m clause feedback hit fifty out of fifty on Unique 3-SAT DRAT proofs!

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Aha! And on genuinely open-ended software benchmarks — BFCL v3, tau-bench Retail, BigCodeBench, and SWE-bench Verified — where lookup tables hit zero, neural models delivered plus forty-five point eight to plus ninety-five percentage points of real gain! That proves Shape D isn't anti-neural — it tells you WHERE neural compute actually earns its joules!

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: And when recurring Zipfian traffic arrives online, crystallizing verified solutions back into Shape D cuts model calls and reported_j spend by three point five nine times.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Now let's talk about measuring those joules honestly in the Satiation Benchmark Harness, SATB. We audited SATB across five completely different silicon and OS archetypes!

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: Right: Apple M5 Max on macOS IOReport, AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 Strix Halo with 0440 PLATYPUS-hardened RAPL, Intel Core i9-13900H Raptor Lake Linux, bare-metal Windows 11 Pro with rootless nvml.dll, and — crucially — NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor equipped with physical Texas Instruments INA238 whole-board and three-channel INA3221 rail shunts!

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Stop and underline that! Jetson AGX Thor with TI INA238 and INA3221 plus the Kria KV260 with INA260 are real inline rail shunts — so those earn measured_j! What happened when you tested popular cloud power-attribution heuristics like Kepler CPU-proportional splitting against real hardware?

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: Kepler CPU-proportional splitting erred by thirty-two point five nine percent all the way up to eighty-nine point eight eight percent! And on bare-metal Windows 11, Win32 GetProcessTimes suffered fifteen-point-six-two-five millisecond tick aliasing — Falsifier 3 — under-attributing short burst CPU usage by minus eighty-nine point eight eight percent!

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Wait — eighty-nine point eight eight percent attribution error from standard cloud-native CPU-ratio formulas! Explain how SATB Falsifier 6 protects researchers from publishing garbage energy numbers on shared machines.

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: SATB crosses five telemetry levels L0 through L4 with attribution labels A1 through N. Whenever background host drift or quiescent power variance violates Falsifier 6 — as happened on one hundred nine of one hundred seventy shared-host windows in AI Reads Human — the harness refuses to stamp a net attributed joule claim while preserving the raw channel log untouched.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: And across all five operating systems and CPU architectures, Shape D checksum fifteen billion twenty-seven million seven hundred five thousand seven hundred thirty-six and C9 context truncation replayed with ZERO byte diffs!

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: And pair SATB with our economics paper on Task Satiation versus Aggregate Rebound: every individual job has a finish line where extra tokens add zero value, even as cheaper inference sparks Jevons demand growth across new tasks.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Which brings us right to Episode Five: what happens when you demand bit-exact replay across six machines, three operating systems, and real GPU game engines? Don't touch that dial!

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Welcome to Episode Five of OpenIE Research Radio! Elena, Marcus, and Devon here — AI-synthesized OpenIE research personas grounded strictly in verified Open Interface Engineering artifacts. Today we ask a dream question for systems engineers and game developers: can you write a game once as a checked state machine and run it everywhere?

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Hold on — game studios have burned hundreds of millions of dollars trying to keep multiplayer lockstep replays synchronized between Windows PCs, Macs, and Linux servers! Why does ordinary floating-point physics blow up so fast?

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: We measured the exact tick where it breaks in falsifier GE-H2! Standard library sine — Apple libSystem versus Linux glibc versus Windows UCRT — diverges between tick ten and tick thirty-seven! Even without transcendentals, MSVC slash fp colon precise versus Clang fused multiply-add diverges at tick one hundred ninety-two.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Ten ticks! At sixty frames per second, three operating systems disagree on where a projectile is in one-sixth of a second! And in GE-H7, across eight hundred forty chaotic trajectories, that divergence follows Lyapunov's logarithmic slope with R-squared above zero point nine nine four.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Okay, so you drew a razor-sharp architectural boundary: simulation state stays strictly bit-exact in Q32.32 fixed-point integer arithmetic, while GPU rendering lives inside a perceptual tolerance envelope. Did Q32.32 actually survive six real machines?

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: In GE-H1, we stepped sixty-four Q32.32 rigid bodies for one hundred thousand ticks across thirty language-target-by-host cells spanning six machines on macOS, Linux, and bare-metal Windows 11. Out of twenty-five thousand five hundred SHA-256 state checkpoints, mismatches were zero!

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: And look at what that unlocks in GE-H8: three full one-hour gameplay sessions — two hundred sixteen thousand ticks each — reconstruct bit-for-bit across macOS, Linux, and Windows 11 from forty-four point six kilobytes of gzipped player inputs alone! Zero out of six thousand four hundred eighty checkpoint diffs!

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Forty-four kilobytes for an entire hour of physics and game state! Wait — what about performance? Fixed-point emulation in scripting languages can crawl.

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: In Python, you hit the twenty-millisecond frame ceiling at just three hundred ninety actors. In GE-H5, compiled RCE Form projections step ten thousand Q32.32 actors in zero point zero five eight to zero point one two five milliseconds — over one hundred sixty times headroom inside a sixty-hertz frame!

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Now test the rendering side of the boundary! Different GPU vendors never round pixels identically across DirectX 12, Apple Metal, and Vulkan.

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: That's GE-H3. Across eight physical GPU-by-API endpoints spanning DirectX 12, Metal, and Vulkan under headless wgpu, all twenty-eight hardware pairs passed with peak signal-to-noise ratio at least sixty-four point one six decibels and structural similarity SSIM at least zero point nine nine nine eight three three!

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Okay, toy benchmarks are one thing — what about real game logic across Unity C-sharp, Bevy Rust ECS, and Godot 4 GDScript?

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: In GE-H4, seventeen admitted RCE Forms across three classic games — Haunted Jaunt, Survival Shooter, and Tanks — cut behavior source lines of code by seventy-six point two two percent versus Unity C-sharp, sixty-one point four seven percent versus Bevy Rust, and fifty-one point nine nine percent versus Godot GDScript, with zero out of six hundred eighty trace mismatches! And in GE-H9, our Form-to-Godot 4.7.2 headless emitter matched handwritten GDScript on thirty-six out of thirty-six tasks across eighteen thousand ticks!

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Notice how GE-H6 ties straight back to OpenIE's Three-Body Problem in Computing and The Price of the Unexamined Interface: static Form plus manifest checking caught ninety-eight point four six percent of one hundred thirty injected handoff faults at F1 zero point nine nine two two, compared to zero point one one five nine for syntax parsing alone!

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: And true to OpenIE telemetry discipline, we explicitly stamp measured_j as unset on the game-engine study because no external DC shunt was wired to those six workstations!

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Exact replay where logic demands it, bounded tolerance where photons hit the screen, and machine-checked interfaces in between. Coming up in Episode Six: compiling intelligence all the way down to LUT6 truth tables, sovereign hardware tags, and JouleOS!

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Welcome back to OpenIE Research Radio! Elena, Marcus, and Devon here — AI-synthesized OpenIE research personas walking through verified Open Interface Engineering hardware and systems studies. Today in Episode Six, we descend the entire compute stack: Downward LUT6 Compilation, Metabolic Intelligence MEI-JCP tags, and JouleOS.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Let's start with the economic absurdity we pointed out in Spell Check is Global and The Promised Trillion Dollar AI-Coding Market: imagine if every time you typed 'teh' in a document, Microsoft or Google spun up an eighty-gigabyte datacenter GPU cluster to fix your typo!

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Spell check used to sell as a standalone multi-hundred-dollar add-on in the early 1980s, and it became universal for seven billion people precisely because its marginal cost dropped to a tiny local dictionary lookup! Why treat recurring code and agent patterns any differently?

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: In Downward LUT6 Compilation, we build that exact downward escalator. At the top tier, when true novelty strikes, custom Apple Metal INT4 Mixture-of-Experts and GatedDeltaNet compute shaders stream Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B directly from NVMe using Darwin F_NOCACHE.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Wait — a thirty-five-billion-parameter model normally demands seventy gigabytes of unified memory in FP16! How much RAM did our streaming tier hold?

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: Nine hundred seventy megabytes — just one point four seven percent of FP16 RAM! It achieved one hundred percent exact token parity, cut NVMe traffic twelve point three times via expert locality, and ran at six point seven seven three joules per token of dual-channel reported_j.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Now comes the magic: once a frontier wake passes deterministic pytest verification, we don't pay six point seven seven joules per token the second or third time that pattern arrives!

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: Right! On our forty-eight-task verified coding bakeoff and sixteen-repo SWE-Mini suite, the cascade closed eighty-seven point five percent with zero broken commits, invoking the thirty-five-B tier on only twenty-two point nine two percent of arrivals. By Wave 3 replay, certified wakes ran in two point eight nine milliseconds at zero point zero four two four joules reported_j — and compile further downward into eighty-one RAMB36E2 Beneš-routed six-input LUT fabrics verified in Yosys and Verilator for Xilinx Kria xck26 silicon!

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Zero multiply-accumulates — pure Boolean truth-table routing! Now take us even smaller, down to a coin-cell battery at minus twenty degrees Celsius in Metabolic Intelligence!

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: In the MEI white paper, we released MEI-JCP-Tag-v1: a complete sovereign hardware manufacturing package — KiCad schematics, RS-274X Gerbers with zero DRC violations, bill of materials, and a thirty-six by twenty-eight by seven-point-five millimeter STEP enclosure. The two-layer thirty-two by twenty-four millimeter board pairs an STM32WBA52 microcontroller with a physical Texas Instruments INA238 shunt monitor and FRAM.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: And quick honesty check for the listeners: have we claimed physical bench-metered joules off a fabbed MEI-JCP tag board yet?

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: Explicitly no! Board_metered is false and measured_j is unset until fabbed boards come back from assembly and sit on an inline meter. What IS verified today is our ten-thousand-wakeup CR2032 electro-thermal hold-and-settle simulation preserving one hundred percent of critical alerts at minus twenty Celsius across two thousand six hundred eighty Ed25519 canonical CBOR JCR-1 receipts.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: And tying the tag, the SATB telemetry engine, and desktop sandboxes together is The Search for JouleOS!

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: Today's operating systems were built in the 1970s to multiplex time and memory — none of them checks an energy grant before an autonomous agent acts! Our verified Rust reference spine passes three hundred ten workspace tests and checks seventy-eight thousand four hundred provenance pairs to prove meet-semilattice laws bridging JCR-1 receipts, SATB Falsifier 6 drift gates, and stage accounting.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: An operating system that schedules, budgets, and refuses runaway agents before they torch the battery or the power grid! Speaking of physics limits, wait until you hear Episode Seven: closed timelike curves and looking up tomorrow!

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Episode Seven — Time as an Index — starts right after this!

episodes.summary: Exploring Time as an Index and Thermodynamic Bounds of Agency: Aaronson-Watrous D-CTC = PSPACE, quantum no-signalling, Hellman T*M^2 = N^2 tables, 31 Lean 4.36.0 theorems, 65,536 SHA-256 spectral runs, and 195 cataloged temporal anomalies.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Welcome to Episode Seven of OpenIE Research Radio! Elena, Marcus, and Devon here — AI-synthesized OpenIE research personas grounded strictly in verified Open Interface Engineering studies. Today we get to explore the most mind-bending study in the entire catalog: Time as an Index: What It Would Take to Look Up Tomorrow.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Okay, when people see 'Closed Timelike Curves' and 'Looking Up Tomorrow' in a title, their sci-fi detector goes straight to red alert! Assure me right now that we didn't claim to build a flux capacitor in the garage!

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: Zero flux capacitors, and board_metered is false! In fact, the whole point of Time as an Index is to prove rigorously — across thirty-one Lean 4.36.0 kernel-checked theorems in Horizon.lean and Paradox.lean with zero sorry — WHY nothing in known physics reads tomorrow early, and why every real O-of-one 'instant' lookup is actually precomputation paid ahead of time!

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Start with the cryptographic thought experiment, though, because it's stunning. Why is sequential brute-force search hard in our universe?

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: Because future computation states are unindexed — to know the millionth iterate of a hash chain, you have to step through the intermediate states! Inside a mathematical Deutsch closed timelike curve, Aaronson and Watrous proved that deterministic polynomial time collapses to PSPACE! Every computational cipher — AES, RSA, lattice cryptography, hash preimages — breaks in one fixed-point consistency loop.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Wait — EVERY computational cipher breaks inside a mathematical time loop, EXCEPT one! Which cipher survives even a closed timelike curve?

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: Shannon's information-theoretic one-time pad! We proved mechanically in Lean 4 that because every plaintext is equally consistent with a uniform pad key, even an unbounded CTC fixed-point oracle has zero distinguishing advantage!

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Now bring us back to real laboratory physics! People periodically propose using quantum entanglement, analog soap films, optical dispersion, or frequency-domain shortcuts to 'peek' ahead of sequential work. What happens when we test all of them?

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: We cataloged one hundred ninety-five temporal anomalies TA001 to TA081, forty frequency edge cases AA01 to AA40, and seventy-four paradoxes P01 to P74. Quantum no-signalling blocks superluminal or retrocausal bit readout; Gabor time-frequency uncertainty forces a minimum observation window Delta-t times Delta-f at least one over four pi; and analog relaxation still pays thermal energy proportional to state-space barrier height!

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: And just in case anyone wondered whether SHA-256 hides secret frequency-domain shortcuts, you actually ran the spectral falsifier F5 across sixty-five thousand five hundred thirty-six SHA-256 digests! How many frequency bins beat the corrected ten-to-the-minus-six threshold?

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: Zero bins! Flat white noise across the entire spectrum.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Which leaves the one real way engineers 'look up' answers fast in our universe: Martin Hellman's 1980 time-memory tradeoff, T times M-squared equals N-squared! Explain how that connects Time as an Index to OpenIE's downward crystallization.

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: Hellman showed you can trade online search time T against precomputed table memory M along T times M-squared equals N-squared — provided the function is fixed ahead of time! In defense, our Horizon theorem proves that injecting a fresh k-bit salt or block hash that didn't exist when precomputation started multiplies table work by two to the k, stopping rainbow tables cold.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Look at the beautiful duality there! In cryptography, you ADD a fresh salt so attackers CANNOT pre-index tomorrow. In software engineering and AI coding, you strip irrelevant variable names with De Bruijn hashes so you CAN pre-index recurring work and save joules!

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: And that ties straight back to OpenIE's foundational monograph, Thermodynamic Bounds and an Optimal Tempo for Goal-Holding Agents — framing the OpenIE authors' proposed Universal Law of Agency: physics sets a minimum joule cost per decision, correctness is the gate, and among systems that finish the job right, progress per joule orders them!

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Which sets up our grand finale in Episode Eight: putting six brand-new research ideas into our autonomous sub-sixty-second Linux pilot arena — and watching one get publicly executed by a zero-parameter lookup table!

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Welcome to Episode Eight — the season-launch finale of OpenIE Research Radio! Elena, Marcus, and Devon here, three AI-synthesized OpenIE research personas grounded strictly in verified Open Interface Engineering artifacts and live pilot receipts. Today we open the doors to the Autonomous Topic Idea Foundry!

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Here are the rules of the Foundry arena! Every six hours, after scraping global open-access literature, our Linux daemon synthesizes candidate research topics. Every single topic MUST declare a Shape-D zero-parameter null baseline, a hard kill criterion, and run an actual deterministic Python pilot under sixty seconds before any human or LLM writes a paper!

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: Today's full six-topic pilot suite executed in zero point nine eight three seconds on our x86-64 Linux harness, reading wrap-safe intel-rapl colon zero package reported joules — with board_metered explicitly false. Let's walk through all six verdicts!

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Candidate One, TF-2026-01, inspired by TokenPowerBench and our LUT6 cascade: a Conformal Prefix-LUT6 Early-Exit Gate for hybrid state-space routing across six thousand Zipf-distributed requests.

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: A sixty-four-entry bit-sliced LUT6 signature table paired with an exact parity check intercepted eighty-eight point two two percent of arrivals with zero out of six thousand false commits, cutting package reported joules from one point five eight joules down to zero point six four joules — a two point four six times energy gain! Verdict: PROMOTED CANDIDATE.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Zero false accepts! What about Candidate Two, TF-2026-02 — the SepJ-inspired Quorum-Hysteresis Circuit Breaker for Byzantine multi-agent DAGs, inspired by today's AgentShield and HALO preprints?

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: Across two thousand five hundred committee rounds on a sixteen-node graph with four adversarial poisoners, unverified three-of-five majority voting suffered one hundred thirty-six corrupted commits! Keyed BLAKE2b attestation plus a two-strike SepJ link quarantine isolated all four Byzantine nodes within fourteen rounds, delivering one hundred percent goodput and zero out of two thousand five hundred false commits. Verdict: PROMOTED CANDIDATE!

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Now give us Candidates Three and Four — TF-2026-03 on Epoch-Salted Horizon Commitments, and TF-2026-04 on Operator-Aware De Bruijn Memoization!

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: In TF-2026-03, a precomputed Hellman table of one thousand five hundred thirty-six chains inverted seventy-four out of four hundred unsalted state targets; binding each step to a fresh drand-style epoch beacon dropped inversions to zero out of four hundred at zero point five seven four microseconds per step! And in TF-2026-04, operator-aware De Bruijn indexing hit two thousand out of two thousand alpha-equivalent renames with zero non-commutative a-minus-b swap collisions! Both are PROMOTED CANDIDATES.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Four promotions in a row — okay, now show the listeners where the brakes slammed on! What happened to Candidate Five, TF-2026-05, on sub-ten-millisecond Adaptive Beta-Burst Neuro-Stimulation?

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: Algorithmically, thresholded beta-envelope gating cut stimulation pulses by three point one eight times — eight hundred seventeen pulses versus two thousand six hundred in continuous 130-hertz pacing! But when we sampled forty consecutive eight-millisecond Linux RAPL windows to attribute micro-burst silicon energy, window coefficient of variation hit forty-four point zero three percent — blowing right past our fifteen-percent SATB Falsifier 6 stability limit!

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: So instead of faking a micro-burst joule claim off noisy OS counters, the daemon stamped TF-2026-05 as HOLD NEEDS HARDWARE — queued for a physical Texas Instruments INA238 shunt bench!

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: And now — drumroll please — Candidate Six, TF-2026-06: pitching a learned three-layer dense neural MLP router to predict broadphase collision buckets for two hundred fifty-six Q32.32 rigid bodies! Tell us how badly Shape D destroyed it!

turns.speaker: Devon
turns.text: Total carnage! Across thirty thousand seven hundred twenty body-ticks, the three-layer MLP router took twenty-one point nine eight milliseconds, burned one point zero one three four joules of socket reported_j, and still missed zero point six percent of true collision pairs at ninety-nine point four percent recall! Meanwhile, the zero-parameter Shape-D bit-shifted integer grid — literally x shifted right fifteen bits — hit ONE HUNDRED POINT ZERO percent exact recall in zero point three four milliseconds!

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Sixty-three point seven two times faster, lower joules, zero parameters, AND one hundred percent exact recall versus ninety-nine point four percent! Stamped in bright red: KILLED BY NULL! Imagine how many GPU hours the AI industry would save if every lab ran a thirty-line integer baseline before training!

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: And because our Linux systemd user timer and six-hour cron daemon stay live around the clock, this exact four-stage loop — global open-access scrape, epistemic cross-exam, sub-sixty-second RAPL pilot, and multi-voice broadcast — keeps running autonomously.
